subject: general
question:
Which line best explains changes in the size of the ozone hole over the years?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64254318f5f59c38514c497b27c6301621b97fd5e9f14b91f6961de1742a7ae6.png]

options.text: Line D - it was growing but now it is shrinking
Line A - it was growing but now it is not growing
Line C - it is growing steadily
Line B - the size has not changed

solution:
The correct answer is __**Line A - it was growing but now it is not growing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Line A indicates that the size of the ozone hole was increasing previously.
 
• The size has stabilized and is no longer expanding.
 
• This implies that the **efforts to reduce the factors causing the ozone depletion have been effective**.
 
• Monitoring the size of the ozone hole is crucial for understanding the effectiveness of environmental policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Hole:**

 
 
• The ozone hole refers to the region over Antarctica where the concentration of ozone in the stratosphere is significantly reduced during certain times of the year.
 
• This phenomenon was first observed in the late 1970s and has been a major environmental concern ever since.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Ozone Depletion:**
 
 
• Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), halons, and other ozone-depleting substances (ODS) are the primary causes of ozone depletion.
 
• These substances release chlorine and bromine atoms upon exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light, which then break down ozone molecules.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol:**
 
 
• The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty adopted in 1987 to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances.
 
• It has been successful in reducing the emissions of ODS and has contributed to the stabilization of the ozone layer.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Ozone Depletion:**
 
 
• Ozone depletion leads to higher levels of harmful UV radiation reaching the Earth's surface.
 
• This can cause increased cases of skin cancer, cataracts, and other health issues, as well as negatively affect ecosystems and wildlife.
